# Singletons

A singleton is a class designed to share one instance.
In robjc, declare it with `RSSingletonClass()` and access the shared object through `Class$instance`.
After declaration, repeated calls to `Class$new()` return that same instance.

For factory arguments and how to choose among factories, see the [class factories guide](guide_05_ClassFactory.Rmd).

## Why use a singleton?

For an ordinary class, each call to `$new()` creates a different object.
If different parts of an application need the same registry, separate instances would hold separate entries.
A single shared instance lets every user see the same state.

Shared mutable state is not the only reason.
`RSNull` shares one object representing null so that code can recognize it by identity.
A singleton also fits something for which **being the one shared object** is itself meaningful.

The instance belongs to the class generator in one R session.
It is not shared across separate R sessions.

## Define a singleton class

`RSSingletonClass()` calls `$new()` once while declaring the class to create the shared instance.
A custom `initialize()` must therefore work without arguments.
It should call `super$initialize()` and return `self`.
Later calls to `$new()` return the stored `Class$instance` without running `initialize()` again.

```{r}
library(robjc)

initializations <- 0L
Registry <- RSSingletonClass(
  "Guide04Registry",
  public = list(
    initialize = function() {
      super$initialize()
      initializations <<- initializations + 1L
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

stopifnot(identical(initializations, 1L))
stopifnot(identical(Registry$new(), Registry$instance))
stopifnot(identical(Registry$new(), Registry$new()))
stopifnot(identical(initializations, 1L))
```

Use `Registry$instance` where you want to make the shared identity explicit.

## `copy()` and the shared instance

As a rule, a singleton's `copy()` returns `self` instead of creating another instance.
Creating a new instance for each copy would break the class's promise to share one object.

The default `copy()` inherited from `RSObject` already returns `self`.
If you override `copy()`, it should normally use `return(self)` as well.

```{r}
stopifnot(identical(Registry$instance$copy(), Registry$instance))
```

Calling `copy()` on a mutable singleton therefore does not create an independent snapshot.
Both references see the same state.

## A singleton in robjc

`RSNull` is a singleton class.
`RSNull$instance` and `RSNull$null` refer to the same object, and `RSNull$new()` returns it too.

```{r}
stopifnot(identical(RSNull$instance, RSNull$null))
stopifnot(identical(RSNull$new(), RSNull$null))
```

The [RSNull technical guide](tech_05_RSNull.Rmd) explains its special behavior when a method is not defined.

## Relationship to ordinary classes and protocols

Use an ordinary `RSObjectClass()` when you need multiple instances with separate state.
Choose a singleton when users should share one object representing the same state or role.

A singleton class can also declare protocol adoption.
In the next example, the shared registry adopts a contract requiring `name()`.
See the [protocols guide](guide_03_Protocols.Rmd) for the purpose and use of protocols.

```{r}
Named <- RSProtocolClass(
  "Guide04Named",
  contract_methods = "name"
)
NamedRegistry <- RSSingletonClass(
  "Guide04NamedRegistry",
  protocols = list(Named),
  public = list(name = function() "shared registry")
)
stopifnot(NamedRegistry$instance$conformsTo(Named))
stopifnot(identical(NamedRegistry$instance$name(), "shared registry"))
```
